My story

Sailing has always been more than a profession.

I'm Salva Durán, a professional sailor and Florida-licensed yacht broker based in Miami. Over more than 25 years, I've sailed in the Mediterranean, the Bay of Biscay, the Caribbean and along the U.S. East Coast — aboard monohulls and catamarans, for work and for the simple pleasure of being at sea.

Deliveries, cruising, racing and time spent living aboard have taught me that a boat is never just a set of specifications. It's where you make decisions, solve problems, share experiences and sometimes call home.

The right boat isn't necessarily the biggest or newest. It's the one that fits the life you want to live.

Life aboard

Our Caribbean chapter.

My wife, CC, and I bought a Jeanneau 45 in Grenada and made it our home. Together we sailed throughout the Caribbean, discovering what living aboard really means — not just the beautiful anchorages, but the everyday realities of maintaining a boat, planning passages and adapting to life afloat.

After COVID, we sold our Jeanneau and moved to Miami. That chapter remains central to the way I advise buyers today, especially couples and families considering their own cruising adventure.

I've lived the questions that many new owners are asking.

From sailing to brokerage

Experience that changes the buying conversation.

My years on the water eventually led me into yacht brokerage, where I've worked with buyers, sellers and yacht builders, including experience with the Fountaine Pajot and Dufour ranges.

Today, I help clients compare both monohulls and catamarans, understand the used-boat market and work through the purchase process. We start with the owner's plans: where they'll sail, who will join them, how they'll use the boat and what ownership will involve.

I work personally with each client. The goal isn't to sell a particular boat; it's to find the right one for the project.

Beyond the purchase

I don't disappear after the handover.

Buying the boat is a milestone, not the finish line. I can help owners and crews prepare for the sailing that comes next.

Owner familiarization, systems, passage preparation and hands-on training — including preparing captains and teams for offshore passages.

Remote support & offshore planning

Sometimes the best help comes from ashore.

Not every question requires someone physically aboard. I also help owners, captains and crews remotely with route planning, weather interpretation, passage preparation and practical decisions before they set off.

That support is particularly valuable when a crew is preparing for a longer passage, navigating unfamiliar waters or simply wants another experienced perspective on its plan.

It's another way to stay connected after the purchase — while the captain on board remains responsible for navigational decisions and safety.

A lifelong passion

From windsurfing to offshore sailing and regattas.

I love the competitive side of sailing too — from windsurf racing to regattas aboard different classes of sailboats.

My sailing experience includes events such as the Copa del Rey in Palma de Mallorca and international 6 Metre class racing. Competition teaches attention to detail, teamwork and respect for the sea — qualities that carry into cruising and professional sailing.

One person, one project

Personal advice. Real sailing experience.

Duran Yachts is intentionally personal. When you work with me, you're speaking directly with the person helping you define your project, evaluate boats, negotiate and prepare for ownership.

Whether your plan involves a cruising monohull, a family catamaran, living aboard or offshore passages, we'll begin with what you want to do — not with a boat I'm trying to sell.

And if you need help once the boat is yours, we can talk about that too.
